#!/bin/bash
# Build an Nxeon GOLDEN game template on THIS Proxmox node.
#
# What a golden template is (docs/DOCUMENTATION.md, "Provisioning pipeline &
# golden templates"): the stock Ubuntu 24.04 template (9000) with everything a
# game provision would otherwise download on every first boot already inside
# it — qemu-guest-agent, unzip/git/curl, Docker CE, and the hottest game images
# pre-pulled. provision() clones it instead of 9000 for game orders when
# NXEON_GOLDEN_GAME_TEMPLATE=<vmid> is set AND this node actually has that
# template (it falls back to 9000 per node otherwise), so it can be rolled out
# one node at a time.
#
# Run ON the target node as root:
#   scripts/golden/build-golden-template.sh <vmid 9100-9199> <build-ip> [disk-size] [images...]
# e.g.
#   scripts/golden/build-golden-template.sh 9101 10.20.1.251 6G \
#       itzg/minecraft-server:java21 itzg/minecraft-server:java25 lloesche/valheim-server
#
# Safety rules this enforces (CLAUDE.md "Safety rules" + the never-reuse-VMIDs rule):
#   - VMID must be in 9100-9199 (the golden range) and must NOT exist on this node
#     or appear anywhere in this node's task history. It is the OPERATOR's job to
#     also check the other 4 nodes — set NXEON_FLEET_HOSTS="ip1 ip2 ..." and the
#     script checks them over ssh too and refuses on any hit.
#   - Never touches 9000/9001 (they are only ever the clone SOURCE).
#   - build-ip must be OUTSIDE the node's allocator pool (.100-.250) and unanswered.
#   - The build VM runs once, powers itself off, and is converted to a template;
#     on any failure it is left STOPPED (not destroyed) for inspection.
set -euo pipefail

VMID=${1:?vmid (9100-9199)}
BUILD_IP=${2:?build ip on vmbr1, outside .100-.250}
DISK=${3:-6G}
shift 3 || true
IMAGES=("$@")
if [ ${#IMAGES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  IMAGES=(itzg/minecraft-server:java21 itzg/minecraft-server:java25 lloesche/valheim-server)
fi
SRC=${NXEON_GOLDEN_SOURCE:-9000}
STORAGE=${NXEON_GOLDEN_STORAGE:-vmdata}
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)

die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

[[ "$VMID" =~ ^91[0-9][0-9]$ ]] || die "vmid must be 9100-9199 (golden range)"
[ "$VMID" != "$SRC" ] || die "vmid equals source"
[[ "$BUILD_IP" =~ ^10\.20\.[0-9]+\.(25[1-4])$ ]] || die "build ip must be 10.20.N.251-254 (outside the allocator pool)"
for img in "${IMAGES[@]}"; do
  [[ "$img" =~ ^[a-z0-9./_-]+(:[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)?$ ]] || die "image ref not allowlisted: $img"
done
[[ "$DISK" =~ ^[0-9]+G$ ]] || die "disk size must look like 6G"

# --- never-reuse-VMIDs: this node, its task history, and (optionally) the fleet ---
vmid_seen_here() {
  ls /etc/pve/nodes/*/qemu-server/"$1".conf /etc/pve/nodes/*/lxc/"$1".conf >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
  cat /var/log/pve/tasks/index* 2>/dev/null | grep -qE ":(qm|vz)[a-z]+:$1:" && return 0
  return 1
}
vmid_seen_here "$VMID" && die "vmid $VMID exists or existed on this node — pick a brand-new one"
for h in ${NXEON_FLEET_HOSTS:-}; do
  if ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 "root@$h" \
      "ls /etc/pve/nodes/*/qemu-server/$VMID.conf >/dev/null 2>&1 || cat /var/log/pve/tasks/index* 2>/dev/null | grep -qE ':(qm|vz)[a-z]+:$VMID:'"; then
    die "vmid $VMID exists or existed on $h — pick a brand-new one"
  fi
done
[ -n "${NXEON_FLEET_HOSTS:-}" ] || echo "WARNING: NXEON_FLEET_HOSTS unset — only THIS node was checked for vmid $VMID."

ping -c1 -W1 "$BUILD_IP" >/dev/null 2>&1 && die "build ip $BUILD_IP answers ping — in use"
qm config "$SRC" | grep -q '^template: 1' || die "source $SRC is not a template on this node"

GW="${BUILD_IP%.*}.1"
SRC_CICUSTOM=$(qm config "$SRC" | sed -n 's/^cicustom: //p')
SNIP_STORE=$(echo "$SRC_CICUSTOM" | sed -n 's/^vendor=\([^:]*\):.*/\1/p')
[ -n "$SNIP_STORE" ] || die "could not read the source template's cicustom vendor storage"
SNIP_DIR="$(pvesm path "$SNIP_STORE:snippets/x.yaml" 2>/dev/null | sed 's#/x.yaml$##')"
[ -d "$SNIP_DIR" ] || die "snippet dir for storage $SNIP_STORE not found"
SNIP="nxeon-golden-build-$VMID.yaml"

sed "s#__IMAGES__#${IMAGES[*]}#" "$HERE/golden-build.yaml" > "$SNIP_DIR/$SNIP"
chmod 600 "$SNIP_DIR/$SNIP"

t0=$(date +%s)
echo "[golden] cloning $SRC -> $VMID on $STORAGE"
qm clone "$SRC" "$VMID" --name "tpl-ubuntu-2404-game" --full 1 --storage "$STORAGE"
qm set "$VMID" --cores 2 --memory 2048 --balloon 0 --nameserver "1.1.1.1 8.8.8.8" \
  --ipconfig0 "ip=$BUILD_IP/24,gw=$GW" --cicustom "vendor=$SNIP_STORE:snippets/$SNIP" >/dev/null
qm resize "$VMID" scsi0 "$DISK" >/dev/null
qm start "$VMID"

echo "[golden] building (waiting for the guest to power itself off, max 25 min)"
deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 1500 ))
while [ "$(qm status "$VMID" | awk '{print $2}')" != "stopped" ]; do
  if [ "$(date +%s)" -gt "$deadline" ]; then
    echo "[golden] TIMEOUT — build log follows; VM $VMID left running for inspection" >&2
    qm guest exec "$VMID" -- tail -50 /var/log/nxeon-golden-build.log >&2 || true
    exit 1
  fi
  sleep 10
done
echo "[golden] guest powered off after $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s"

# Restore the source template's cloud-init shape (static vendor snippet with
# ssh_pwauth + guest-agent startup), drop build-only settings, convert.
qm set "$VMID" --delete ipconfig0,nameserver,balloon --cicustom "$SRC_CICUSTOM" \
  --cores 1 --memory 1024 --tags "nxeon-golden" \
  --description "Nxeon golden game template. Built $(date -u +%FT%TZ) from $SRC. Images: ${IMAGES[*]}" >/dev/null
qm template "$VMID"
rm -f "$SNIP_DIR/$SNIP"
echo "[golden] template $VMID ready ($(qm config "$VMID" | sed -n 's/^scsi0: //p'))"

Wait, node-5's listing shows configs 142 and 143 again, which conflicts with those being destroyed earlier—it seems the platform may have reused those IDs when the coordinator provisioned new VMs on bhs1.

This confirms the bug: recycled IDs from yesterday's destroyed VMs are getting reused by a new sweep right now, alongside existing hosting VMs on other nodes. The fix is a high-water-mark approach: compute the next fresh VMID as the max of the stored next-VMID setting and one more than the highest existing DB VMID below 9000, so I need a function that takes the current next-VMID and all ever-used VMIDs, filters out the template range and any sandbox-range IDs (990000+), and returns a safe floor above all historical and current VMIDs.

If that floor happens to land inside the 9000-9999 template range, I bump it up to 10000 to avoid colliding with templates. Then the allocation function probes upward from that floor, treating the whole 9000-9999 range as always taken so it never wanders into template territory, and after a successful allocation I persist the new high-water mark (only if it's higher than before) -- with the database's unique constraint on Server.vmid as the final safety net against race conditions between concurrent provisioning attempts.

Rather than risk a retry eating into the attempt budget, I want to make the high-water-mark bump itself atomic using a single upsert statement that does a GREATEST comparison and returns the new value in one round trip, so two concurrent provisions naturally get distinct candidates without a race window.

I still need to handle the template-ID-range special case by re-checking the returned candidate and bumping the floor to 10000 if it lands in the 9000-9999 reserved band, plus finalize the real chosen vmid back into the setting after pickProvisionVmid resolves conflicts. This feels like a legitimate, surgical fix for a real correctness gap rather than overengineering.

Now I'm sketching the implementation plan: a pure helper module for golden-template logic (functions to find the golden template vmid, decide whether to use it, and parse disk size from config), an async resolver in the worker to pick the right clone source, and small tweaks to the cloud-init builder to accept a golden option. Time to start writing the actual code in worker/index.ts, beginning with the clone source logic.

I'm noting that the reinstall fields selection likely won't include gamePlan, so a reinstall won't get a ramMB value and heap stays unchanged under catalog behavior — that's fine, just worth flagging. Now I'm starting the game-variant.ts additions, beginning with a function that skips the Docker install step if Docker is already present by replacing the install curl command with a conditional check.

I'm verifying the skip-install replacement preserves the original exit-status semantics and doesn't accidentally match the later docker-run regex, since only "docker" appears in the command-check text, not "docker run" — so it should be safe to apply before the wrapping step, and this only affects game templates since other Docker-based app templates don't go through this script builder. Next I'm defining a function to apply a Minecraft memory heap limit, which only kicks in for the minecraft family when ramMB is a valid positive number and the script already sets a MEMORY env var — I'm working out the max heap calculation by reserving headroom for the OS, roughly subtracting the greater of a fixed 768MB or 25% of total RAM from the total, then flooring to the nearest 256MB.

I'm deciding the logic for whether to auto-size to max heap or respect the user's explicit setting: if the config value is absent or matches the schema's default of "2G", I treat it as auto and use the computed max heap; otherwise I clamp the customer's chosen value to the max heap ceiling, with a 512MB minimum, then substitute it into the MEMORY env assignment. I'm noting this relies on itzg's behavior where MEMORY sets both Xms and Xmx equally, and that I need to parse the value directly from gameConfig since this runs after the generic env substitution step — but I'm second-guessing whether the real game-config worker logic re-applies the customer's raw value afterward in a way that could override this.

For password rotation, I'm defining a set of admin secret env keys to check against a list of weak defaults, replacing any that match with a securely generated value — but this only triggers if the customer never set a custom value, since setting one (even a weak-looking one) removes it from the weak-defaults match, which I'll document as acceptable. The problem is that if we rotate silently, the customer won't know the new password, so I'm thinking the generation needs to happen during provision and get persisted back into gameConfig so it stays discoverable, rather than purely inside the stateless script-building function.

I'm sketching out the flow: before building the cloud-init script, generate passwords for each key that needs rotation, write them into gameConfig when a matching schema field exists so they persist and get substituted normally, and for keys without a schema field, pass them through as extra secrets into the script builder. Simplifying further, I think the cleanest approach is to have the script builder itself regenerate any still-weak default inline (matching the pattern used for palworld), while provision() pre-fills gameConfig ahead of time for any keys with schema fields.

Thinking through retry idempotency, since cloud-init won't re-run on a retry against an existing VM (instance-id stays the same), whatever secrets got generated on the first attempt are what's actually baked into the guest -- so persisted schema-field secrets will match on retry, while non-persisted rotated secrets will differ in what gets regenerated versus what's already running, but since nothing else reads those stored values and the platform just reads the live docker env, it stays consistent either way. /**
 * Side-effect-free pieces of the per-server cloud-init vendor snippet built by
 * `buildCloudInit` (worker/index.ts). Kept here so they can be unit tested —
 * importing worker/index.ts starts the job loop.
 */

/**
 * Packages every VM needs before anything else in the snippet works:
 *   - qemu-guest-agent: provision()'s boot check and every QGA-based feature
 *     (password reset, in-guest disk/memory samples, restore password resync).
 *   - unzip: found live 2026-09-09 — worker/game-mods.ts's zip-type mod
 *     install has always assumed it exists on every game VM, but nothing ever
 *     installed it. Universal (not game-conditional): trivial and useful on a
 *     plain VPS too.
 *
 * On a STOCK cloud image this block stays exactly as it always was. On a
 * GOLDEN template (scripts/golden/build-golden-template.sh) both are already
 * installed, and `package_update: true` alone was the single biggest slice of
 * first boot — measured 2026-10-01 on a stock Ubuntu 24.04 clone:
 * `config-package_update_upgrade_install ran successfully and took 72.150
 * seconds`, i.e. the guest agent could not answer until ~95s after start. So a
 * golden clone emits nothing here.
 *
 * Returns either "" or a block ending in a newline, so the caller can splice
 * it directly in front of the next top-level key.
 */
export function cloudInitPackagesBlock(golden: boolean): string {
  if (golden) return "";
  return ["package_update: true", "packages:", "  - qemu-guest-agent", "  - unzip", ""].join("\n");
}

/**
 * The runcmd line that launches /root/nxeon-setup.sh in the background.
 *
 * The setup script runs under `set -x`, so its log holds every command it
 * ran — including per-server secrets substituted into `docker create -e
 * ADMIN_PASSWORD=…` and the telemetry token. That log used to be created by a
 * plain `>` redirect, i.e. with the default umask: 0644, readable by every
 * local account on the customer's VM (www-data, a database user, a
 * compromised app). Pre-create it 0600 and append to it instead.
 */
export const SETUP_RUNCMD = [
  "  - install -m 600 /dev/null /var/log/nxeon-setup.log",
  "  - nohup /root/nxeon-setup.sh >> /var/log/nxeon-setup.log 2>&1 &",
].join("\n");

Both installs finished with the disk no longer growing, containers quiet, and ports never opening. For Squad, GAME_PORT is set to the RCON port 21114/tcp, but RCON only opens when a password is configured, which it isn't — so the health check is targeting the wrong port entirely. The actual fix needs to check 7787/udp with in-guest bound verification, pointing to lib/games.ts GAME_PORT as the root cause.

For Stationeers, docs confirm it's known unsellable since it never binds any port — this raises an ownership question about whether "known broken" families should be blocked from ordering at all, which isn't my call to decide, just report.

Looking at the retry path: a second provision attempt re-enters with the VM already existing, so it skips cloning but re-POSTs config, attempts a resize to the same size (which may or may not be a no-op depending on Proxmox behavior), skips the start since it's already running, then redoes guest agent wait, SSH, and the 300s port check. Each failed attempt eats 5-8 minutes, so three attempts stretch to 20+ minutes before erroring out — and critically, the VM isn't torn down afterward, consistent with the rule that failed checks shouldn't destroy VMs.

For the stall heuristic, I'm worried that "3 minutes with no disk growth and no output" could false-positive on heavy Unreal games where the world load is CPU-busy but silent. I want to add a CPU-based progress signal by reading cumulative CPU usage from the container's cgroup v2 stats file, falling back to zero if unavailable — this makes the check family-agnostic without relying on game-specific log patterns.

Still, I realize this won't rescue Squad's actual bug: if the probe is hitting the wrong port (RCON instead of game), the server could be fully up and consuming CPU, yet the probe would still wait the full 45 minutes before failing since CPU activity alone can't confirm the right service is listening. So the port fix remains essential regardless of the CPU signal improvement.

Given the time constraints, I'm setting priorities: confirm the typecheck passes, fix the squad GAME_PORT issue plus the CPU-based progress check in waitOutGameInstall, verify the scheduleNode template presence in node-capacity.ts, and then check which families use ports 9001 and 9005-9009 versus the 9000 base.

I need to document the tradeoffs — the template can't be deleted while clones reference it, rebuilds must use fresh vmids, and backups/restores or migrations still produce independent full disks, so none of the existing lifecycle logic breaks. I'll wire this in as a default-off option to keep current behavior safe.

## Troubleshooting — provisioning and the worker

| Symptom | Cause | Fix / where to look |
|---|---|---|
| Button does nothing, no error | One in-flight job per server; a `RUNNING` row blocks every later action | Queue-check SQL in the restart runbook; a worker restart trips `reapStuckJobs` |
| SSL "stuck pending" for many minutes | The worker is a **strictly serial** single-job queue; the cert is behind a long job. One cert sat `PENDING` 13m15s behind a 24-minute migration | Not a bug, a design limit. Queue position is resolved at `app/dashboard/ssl/page.tsx:44` |
| Server stuck `PROVISIONING`/`REINSTALLING`/`DELETING` | Worker died mid-job | `reapStuckJobs()` `worker/index.ts:1113` requeues under 3 attempts, else `ERROR` + reconcile |
| A backup shut the server down | `BACKUP_CREATE` was treated as a VM-state failure | **Fixed** — excluded from `VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS` (`worker/index.ts:50-53`); backups use `mode: "snapshot"`. A failed backup now notifies on its final attempt (`:861-872`) instead of being silent |
| A failed disk expansion marked the server `ERROR` | `DISK_EXPAND` was in the failure set | **Fixed** — deliberately absent (`worker/index.ts:44`); money unwound by `reconcileFailedDiskExpand` (`:822`) |
| Customer holds extra disk; a plan resize hard-fails | Resize computed the target as `plan.diskGB`, i.e. a *shrink* | **Fixed** — worker resizes to `plan.diskGB + extraDiskGB` (`worker/index.ts:559`) |
| Reinstall wiped an attached volume | No guard | **Fixed** — `worker/index.ts:428-448`, `lib/actions.ts:464-471` |
| `RUNNING` but no SSH | Used to be that `status: RUNNING` was written right after Proxmox accepted `start`, proving nothing about the guest | **Improved.** `waitForGuestAgent` (`worker/index.ts:342`) now gates the `RUNNING` write (`:344`), the cloud-init snippet write hard-fails rather than being swallowed (`:286-289`), and a port-forward failure is named as a caveat (`:349-354`) instead of printing an SSH command that would hang. If it is still unreachable: web console first, then `PortForward` vs `iptables -t nat -L NXEON_FWD -n` |
| New server has no IP / VMID | Pool exhausted, or a deleted row still holds the UNIQUE `ipAddress` | `lib/ipam.ts`; release logic `worker/index.ts:988` |
| Staging touched a production VM | Wrong `NXEON_IP_START/END` or `NXEON_NAT_CHAIN` in `/opt/nxeon-staging/.env` | Staging is `.50–.99` / `30000–30999` / `NXEON_FWD_STG` / tag `nxeon-staging`. Nothing else separates them |
| A scheduled thing stopped happening | Every sweep is individually `try`/`catch`ed, so a permanently broken one is silent | grep the journal for `sweep error` |

## Troubleshooting — migration
## Environment variables and feature flags

Set in `/opt/nxeon/.env` (chmod 600, gitignored). **Never commit it; never print the Proxmox token.**

| Group | Variables |
|---|---|
| Core | `DATABASE_URL` `AUTH_SECRET` `APP_URL` `PORT` `COOKIE_SECURE` |
| Proxmox | `PROXMOX_API_URL` `PROXMOX_TOKEN_ID` `PROXMOX_TOKEN_SECRET` `PROXMOX_NODE` `PUBLIC_IP` |
| Stripe | `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` |
| Registrars | `NAMECOM_USERNAME` `NAMECOM_TOKEN` `NAMECOM_ENV`; `NAMECHEAP_API_USER` `NAMECHEAP_API_KEY` `NAMECHEAP_USERNAME` `NAMECHEAP_CLIENT_IP` `NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX` |
| Mail | `MAILCOW_API_URL` `MAILCOW_API_KEY` `SMTP_TLS_SERVERNAME` |
| Cloudflare | `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` `CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` **`CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_SCOPES`** |
| OVH | `OVH_ENDPOINT` `OVH_APPLICATION_KEY` `OVH_APPLICATION_SECRET` `OVH_CONSUMER_KEY` |
| Steam | `STEAM_WEB_API_KEY` (GSLT auto-mint, `lib/steam-gslt.ts`); `DAYZ_STEAM_USERNAME` `DAYZ_STEAM_PASSWORD` — a dedicated, Nxeon-owned, download-only Steam account (Steam Guard deliberately off), needed because DayZ's dedicated-server depot rejects anonymous SteamCMD login unlike every other family. Unset ⇒ `lib/game-order.ts` refuses new DayZ orders outright ("DayZ hosting isn't available yet"). See `lib/dayz-steam.ts` for the full mechanism and the one real manual step (creating that account) — no Steam account exists in this environment to set these for real. |
| Admin / console | `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` `NXEON_ADMIN_HOSTS` `CONSOLE_PUBLIC_WS_URL` |
| Environment split | `NXEON_ENV` `NXEON_COOKIE_NAME` `NXEON_NAT_CHAIN` `NXEON_TAG` `NXEON_IP_START` `NXEON_IP_END` `NXEON_SSH_PORT_START` `NXEON_SSH_PORT_END` `NXEON_CRED_FILE` |

**Feature flags — and what happens when each is off.** This table is the single most important thing
to check when a feature "does nothing".
- **Fix**: new nullable `Server.guestSshPort` column (additive, `db push`'d — changes nothing for any
  existing server, since `null` falls back to `?? 22`, today's exact behavior). `connectionTarget()`'s
  dedicated-IP branch now reads `server.guestSshPort ?? 22` instead of a bare `22`. Selected into
  `lib/actions-files.ts`'s server query (the Files feature); `worker/firewall.ts` already `include`s
  the whole row so it picked it up for free. New unit tests in `test/sftp-connection-target.test.ts`
  pin both the override and the (unchanged) default. Admin server detail page now shows "Guest SSH
  port override" for any server with a dedicated IP, so this doesn't stay a hidden DB-only field.
- **The firewall side needed a second, separate finding**: even with the port fixed, `syncFirewall`
  would still fail — this guest's `iptables` (legacy) returns "Incompatible with this kernel" (likely
  1Panel's own nftables-only setup). Checked the LIVE guest directly: `iptables -L INPUT` showed only
  UFW's own chains (`ufw-before-input` etc.), policy DROP — confirming the platform's `NXEON_FW` chain
  has in fact never once been successfully applied to this guest, so there was nothing live to
  "detach". The customer's 6 stale `FirewallRule` DB rows are display-only leftovers; deleting them
  requires no guest-side sync (and syncing them now would risk appending a default-DROP that doesn't
  know about port 2222 — `FW_KEEP_OPEN_TCP_PORTS` only keeps 22 open — so deliberately did NOT trigger
  a sync). `SYNC_FIREWALL` jobs are only ever created by `lib/actions-firewall.ts` on an explicit rule
  edit (confirmed — no periodic/cron trigger exists), so once those 6 rows are gone, nothing re-fires
  on its own.
- **Not yet done**: deleting the 6 stale `FirewallRule` rows was blocked by the auto-mode permission
  classifier ("Modify Shared Resources") on a direct DB write — needs the owner to run it or grant it.
  Worth a platform-wide follow-up too: any guest running an nftables-only setup (1Panel defaults to
  this) can never successfully use the panel firewall feature at all, independent of this port issue.

**Files:** `prisma/schema.prisma`, `lib/sftp.ts`, `lib/actions-files.ts`,
`app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, `test/sftp-connection-target.test.ts`.

---

*Companion docs: `CLAUDE.md` (agent/ops conventions), `ROADMAP.md` (backlog), `docs/MIGRATION.md`
(server migration).*

## Provisioning pipeline, timings and golden templates

What a `PROVISION` job actually does, where the time goes, and how to make it faster. Measured
2026-10-01 (prod `Job` table + `journalctl -u nxeon-worker` + Proxmox task logs + three timed test
clones on node-5/node-2). Code: `provision()` in `worker/index.ts`, `lib/golden-template.ts`,
`worker/cloud-init-parts.ts`, `worker/game-variant.ts`, `scripts/golden/`.

### The pipeline, in order

| # | Step | Where | Typical time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Queue wait (job `createdAt` → worker picks it up) | worker loop | 0-40s; up to 137s observed while the worker ran 1 job at a time (now `WORKER_CONCURRENCY=8`) |
| 2 | vmid (never-reuse floor), dedicated IP / NAT IP + SSH port, password, DB writes | `allocateFreshVmid`, `lib/ipam.ts` | 1-2s |
| 3 | `qm clone` (full copy) of `OsTemplate.baseVmid` — or a golden template | Proxmox | 4s (node-5 NVMe, stock 3.5 GB) · 24.5s (node-2, stock) · 67.7s (node-2, 4.2 GB golden, full) · **2.1s (node-2, golden, linked)** |
| 4 | Per-VM cloud-init snippet (primary: local file, others: node-agent) + config + resize | Proxmox | ~3s |
| 5 | NAT forward sync (all 5 nodes) | `worker/network.ts` | ~2s |
| 6 | Start | Proxmox | ~1s |
| 7 | Guest-agent wait | `waitForGuestAgent` | was **a fixed 180s on every provision** (bug, see below); now = real boot: ~15s golden, ~90-120s stock |
| 8 | SSH reachability (banner) | `checkSshReachable`, 5s interval | ~15-20s after start |
| 9 | Game port (TCP connect, or UDP + in-guest bound socket) | `checkGamePortOpen` 300s, then `waitOutGameInstall` up to 45 min while the guest shows progress | depends on the game (below) |
| 10 | RUNNING, emails, join-port forwards, admin-port retraction, `SYNC_GAME_DNS`, optional `GAME_CONFIG` | `provision()` tail | ~5s |

Inside the guest (stock Ubuntu 24.04, 2 vCPU / 2 GB, measured on node-5):

| Phase | Time after start |
|---|---|
| sshd answers (key auth) | 23s |
| cloud-init `package_update` + `qemu-guest-agent` + `unzip` | **72.2s** (`config-package_update_upgrade_install`) |
| guest agent up / runcmd starts | 95s |
| Claude CLI install (used to run BEFORE the game) | +10s |
| `get.docker.com` + `itzg/minecraft-server:java21` pull + `docker create` | +25s (stock) · +1.2s (golden) |
| Minecraft world generation → port 25565 open | +30-35s |

### Measured production durations (last 30 days, `PROVISION` jobs, run time excludes queue wait)

| Type / family | n | Run time | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ubuntu VPS | 13 | 193-264s (p50 ~210s) | Proxmox work is ~16s of that; ~180s was the guest-agent bug |
| Minecraft | 7 OK | 199-262s | |
| Bedrock | 2 | 223-228s | |
| Terraria | 1 | 257s | |
| Palworld | 2 | 288s, 1177s (2 attempts) | |
| Core Keeper | 1 | 296s | |
| Project Zomboid | 1 | 372s | |
| Valheim | 7 | 197-579s | |
| Don't Starve Together | 1 | 701s (2 attempts) | needs a customer Klei token |
| ARK | 1 | 1269s | 22.9 GB SteamCMD download |
| Rust | 1 | 1475s (3 attempts) | |
| CS2 | 1 FAILED | 2062s | known-unsellable (66 GB install) |
| All `PROVISION` jobs | 51 DONE / 23 FAILED | p50 353s (DONE) | |

**35 of 35** "server ready" notifications in the 20 days before this fix read *"is up, with caveats …
guest agent has not answered yet"*.

### Bugs found and fixed (2026-10-01)

1. **The guest-agent wait could never succeed.** `waitForGuestAgent` polled `GET …/agent/ping`;
   Proxmox only defines `POST` for `ping` (`pvesh get …/agent/ping` → *No 'get' handler defined*).
   Every poll threw, so every provision waited the full 180s, returned `booted=false`, and told the
   customer "with caveats". The same function gates the password resync after `BACKUP_RESTORE` and
   `SNAPSHOT_ROLLBACK`, which therefore never ran. Now probes `GET …/agent/info` (a real guest-agent
   round trip) every 2s. **Expected effect: ~180s off every VPS provision, ~60-150s off every game
   provision, and honest "ready" notifications.**
2. **Minecraft heap = the whole VM.** The catalog's `-e MEMORY=2G` sets `-Xms`=`-Xmx`=2G; on the 2 GB
   plan the JVM cannot commit its heap without swap ("insufficient memory for the Java Runtime …
   failed to map 2147483648 bytes", crash loop, `NRestarts=78` in 10 min on a no-swap test VM); real
   orders survive only because of the swapfile. On the 8 GB plan the heap stayed 2G. Now
   `applyMinecraftHeap` sizes it to RAM minus max(768 MB, 25%) (2 GB → 1280M, 4 GB → 3072M, 8 GB →
   6144M) and clamps an explicit customer choice to that ceiling. *Not yet mirrored* in
   `worker/game-config.ts`'s post-provision MEMORY apply (R gamestate's area) — a customer who saves
   Settings can still re-apply an oversized value.
3. **Shared admin passwords.** Project Zomboid (`ADMIN_USERNAME=admin ADMIN_PASSWORD=changeme12`), ARK,
   ARK SA, Icarus, Soulmask, L4D2, TF2 shipped the same `changeme12` admin/RCON password on every
   server. Now: a blank customer value over a weak placeholder gets a per-server secret minted once in
   `provision()` and persisted into `Server.gameConfig` (visible in Settings, reused on retry and
   reinstall); admin/RCON env vars with no schema field are rotated per build. Join passwords are
   never touched. Platform RCON reads the password back out of the container env, so it keeps working.
4. **VMIDs were being recycled.** `/cluster/nextid` returns the lowest free id; node-5 destroyed 117 and
   142-145 overnight and handed 117/142/143 straight back out the same day. `allocateFreshVmid` now
   starts from `max(nextid, highest vmid ever on a Server row + 1, Setting vmid_high_water + 1)`,
   claimed atomically (one SQL upsert, safe under `WORKER_CONCURRENCY`), skipping 9000-9999, 200 and
   8000. The first allocation after deploy will be ~601 (current DB max is 600).
5. **Squad could never pass readiness**: `GAME_PORT.squad` was RCON 21114/tcp, which never opens without
   an RCON password. Now 7787/udp (with the in-guest bound-socket check). Found by the 2026-10-01 live
   all-families sweep.
6. **Silent heavy loads were declared stalled.** Squad/Stationeers had a flat disk and no log output
   for 3 minutes while loading. `waitOutGameInstall` now also counts the container cgroup's CPU time
   (≥15s CPU per 60s sample) as progress (`installProgressed`, `GAME_INSTALL_MIN_CPU_USEC`).
7. **Orders scheduled onto nodes without their template.** node-2/node-4 lack 9005-9009, node-5 lacks
   9001 and 9005-9009. `scheduleNode(…, { templateVmid })` now skips them (per-node template list,
   10-min cache, unknown = excluded, admin `logError` naming the nodes). Affected images: Debian 13 +
   Webmin/HestiaCP/CloudPanel (9001), Debian 12 (9005), Ubuntu 20.04 (9006), AlmaLinux 8 (9007),
   Rocky 8 (9008), Debian 11 (9009). **No game family is affected** (all clone 9000).
8. Smaller: game setup runs **before** the Claude CLI install (−10s); `get.docker.com` is skipped when
   Docker already exists (golden templates, `GAME_REINSTALL`); the primary's cloud-init snippets are
   written `0600` (they hold game secrets + the telemetry token; node-agent already did); the `set -x`
   setup log `/var/log/nxeon-setup.log` is pre-created `0600` (it echoes those secrets).

### Golden templates (opt-in, per family, per node)

A golden template = stock 9000 + `qemu-guest-agent`, `unzip`, `git`, `curl`, Docker CE and a few
pre-pulled images, with per-instance identity scrubbed (`cloud-init clean`, empty `/etc/machine-id`,
no SSH host keys, root password locked). A clone boots as a brand-new machine (verified: fresh
machine-id, fresh host keys, cloud-init sets the root password, `cloud-init status: done`).

**Measured, Minecraft 2 GB, node-2, same new snippet both times (from `qm start`):**

| | Stock 9000 | Golden 9101 |
|---|---|---|
| Guest agent | 117s | **15s** |
| SSH | 19.5s | 15.3s |
| Docker image ready | ~67s after setup start | **1.2s** |
| Game port open | 193s | **48s** |
| Clone (node-2) | 24.5s full | 67.7s full / **2.1s linked** |

End to end that is ≈ 220s → ≈ 50-60s with a linked golden clone (plus the 180s agent bug that both
columns no longer pay). Steam families gain proportionally less: their time is dominated by the
SteamCMD download inside the container, which a golden template cannot pre-seed without per-family
server files (see "Next steps").

**How provision() decides** (`chooseCloneSource`): `NXEON_GOLDEN_GAME_TEMPLATE` must map the order's
family to a vmid in 9100-9199 (`9101` = every game; `minecraft:9101,valheim:9101`; `*:9102` wildcard);
the order must be a game whose base is 9000; and the target node must have that vmid **as a template
tagged `nxeon-golden`** whose disk is not larger than the order's disk (Proxmox cannot shrink). Any
miss → stock 9000, logged per provision. Golden clones get a cloud-init snippet without the
`package_update`/`packages` block. `NXEON_GOLDEN_LINKED_CLONE=1` additionally makes golden clones linked
(`full: 0`) when the order's storage is the template's storage.

**Linked clones — the tradeoff.** ~2s instead of 25-70s and no extra space until the guest writes. But
Proxmox refuses to destroy a template that still has linked clones, so a rebuilt golden template always
gets a **new** vmid (9101 → 9102 …, as the never-reuse rule requires anyway), the env mapping is moved to
it, and the old one is destroyed only once `qm list`/`zfs list -t all` shows no clone depends on it.
Backups (`vzdump`) and restores produce independent full disks.

**Building one** (run ON the node, as root; never touches 9000/9001):

```
# 1. pick a vmid in 9100-9199 that has NEVER existed on ANY node (configs + /var/log/pve/tasks/index*)
# 2. pick a build IP 10.20.N.251-254 (outside the allocator pool) that does not answer ping
NXEON_FLEET_HOSTS="<the other 4 node IPs>" scripts/golden/build-golden-template.sh 9101 10.20.1.251 12G \
    itzg/minecraft-server:java21 itzg/minecraft-server:java25 lloesche/valheim-server
```

It clones 9000, boots it once with `scripts/golden/golden-build.yaml`, waits for the guest to power
itself off (25 min cap; on failure the VM is left for inspection), restores 9000's static vendor
`cicustom`, tags it `nxeon-golden`, converts it to a template and removes the build snippet. Disk: 12G
is needed for three images (Docker 29's containerd snapshotter stores compressed + extracted layers; a
6G attempt ran out of space). 12G excludes only plans smaller than that (Bedrock 5 GB, Necesse/CS 1.6
8 GB), which automatically fall back to stock.

**Distributing:** templates are per node. Either run the build script on each node (simplest — each
node gets an identical build), or `vzdump 9101` → copy → `qmrestore … <same vmid> --unique 0` +
`qm template`. Check the vmid fleet-wide first either way. Rebuild weekly (pre-pulled `:latest` images
and apt packages age; `docker create` uses the local image and does not re-pull) — build a new vmid,
move the env mapping, retire the old one when unreferenced.

**Current state (2026-10-01):** POC template **9101 exists on node-2 only** (`tpl-ubuntu-2404-game`,
12G, 4.24 GB used, MC java21+java25 + Valheim images). `NXEON_GOLDEN_GAME_TEMPLATE` is **unset in
prod**, so nothing uses it yet. Rollout = build on each node → set the env (start with
`minecraft:9101,valheim:9101`) → restart the worker → watch the `clone source` log line.

### Next steps (not built)

- **Per-family templates with pre-seeded server files** for the slow Steam families (Rust, ARK,
  Palworld, Valheim server files): a clone would only `steamcmd validate` a delta. Cost: the files live
  on every clone's disk and go stale with each game patch — needs a scheduled rebuild per family.
- **A local Docker registry mirror / Steam depot cache** per node (one pull per node instead of one per
  order). Lower risk than per-family templates; helps every family.
- **Pre-warmed spare VMs** (a booted golden clone per hot game per node, handed out on order): order to
  playable ≈ 10-20s, but each spare holds its RAM 24/7 (2 GB × 3 hot games × 4 nodes ≈ 24 GB of the
  fleet's ~280 GB), must be re-identified (hostname, password, keys, telemetry token) at hand-out, and
  is idle capacity that cannot be sold. Only worth it once golden + linked clones have shipped and the
  remaining ~50s is still the complaint.
- `qm resize` + config + start + NAT sync could overlap the clone wait on other nodes; small (<5s).

entry='''
## Provisioning speed + script audit: the 180s guest-agent wait, heap sizing, shared admin passwords, VMID reuse, golden templates (2026-10-01)

Measured where provisioning time goes (prod `Job` table, worker journal, Proxmox task logs, timed test
clones) and fixed what was found. Full write-up, timings and the golden-template procedure:
"Provisioning pipeline, timings and golden templates".

- `lib/proxmox.ts` `waitForGuestAgent`: `GET agent/ping` (no such handler) → `GET agent/info`, poll 2s.
  Removes a fixed 180s from every provision and the "with caveats" notice from every ready email;
  restore / snapshot-rollback password resync now actually runs.
- `lib/proxmox.ts` `freshVmidFloor` + `worker/index.ts` `claimVmidFloor`: never-reuse vmid allocation
  (atomic `Setting vmid_high_water`), template range / 200 / 8000 never candidates.
- `worker/game-variant.ts`: `applyMinecraftHeap` (heap sized to plan RAM), `skipDockerInstallIfPresent`,
  `adminSecretFieldsToMint` + `rotateWeakAdminSecrets` (no more shared `changeme12` admin/RCON

## Provisioning pipeline, timings and golden templates

What a `PROVISION` job actually does, where the time goes, and how to make it faster. Measured
2026-10-01 (prod `Job` table + `journalctl -u nxeon-worker` + Proxmox task logs + three timed test
clones on node-5/node-2). Code: `provision()` in `worker/index.ts`, `lib/golden-template.ts`,
`worker/cloud-init-parts.ts`, `worker/game-variant.ts`, `scripts/golden/`.

### The pipeline, in order

| # | Step | Where | Typical time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Queue wait (job `createdAt` → worker picks it up) | worker loop | 0-40s; up to 137s observed while the worker ran 1 job at a time (now `WORKER_CONCURRENCY=8`) |
| 2 | vmid (never-reuse floor), dedicated IP / NAT IP + SSH port, password, DB writes | `allocateFreshVmid`, `lib/ipam.ts` | 1-2s |
| 3 | `qm clone` (full copy) of `OsTemplate.baseVmid` — or a golden template | Proxmox | 4s (node-5 NVMe, stock 3.5 GB) · 24.5s (node-2, stock) · 67.7s (node-2, 4.2 GB golden, full) · **2.1s (node-2, golden, linked)** |
| 4 | Per-VM cloud-init snippet (primary: local file, others: node-agent) + config + resize | Proxmox | ~3s |
| 5 | NAT forward sync (all 5 nodes) | `worker/network.ts` | ~2s |
| 6 | Start | Proxmox | ~1s |
| 7 | Guest-agent wait | `waitForGuestAgent` | was **a fixed 180s on every provision** (bug, see below); now = real boot: ~15s golden, ~90-120s stock |
| 8 | SSH reachability (banner) | `checkSshReachable`, 5s interval | ~15-20s after start |
| 9 | Game port (TCP connect, or UDP + in-guest bound socket) | `checkGamePortOpen` 300s, then `waitOutGameInstall` up to 45 min while the guest shows progress | depends on the game (below) |
| 10 | RUNNING, emails, join-port forwards, admin-port retraction, `SYNC_GAME_DNS`, optional `GAME_CONFIG` | `provision()` tail | ~5s |

Inside the guest (stock Ubuntu 24.04, 2 vCPU / 2 GB, measured on node-5):

| Phase | Time after start |
|---|---|
| sshd answers (key auth) | 23s |
| cloud-init `package_update` + `qemu-guest-agent` + `unzip` | **72.2s** (`config-package_update_upgrade_install`) |
| guest agent up / runcmd starts | 95s |
| Claude CLI install (used to run BEFORE the game) | +10s |
| `get.docker.com` + `itzg/minecraft-server:java21` pull + `docker create` | +25s (stock) · +1.2s (golden) |
| Minecraft world generation → port 25565 open | +30-35s |

### Measured production durations (last 30 days, `PROVISION` jobs, run time excludes queue wait)

| Type / family | n | Run time | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ubuntu VPS | 13 | 193-264s (p50 ~210s) | Proxmox work is ~16s of that; ~180s was the guest-agent bug |
| Minecraft | 7 OK | 199-262s | |
| Bedrock | 2 | 223-228s | |
| Terraria | 1 | 257s | |
| Palworld | 2 | 288s, 1177s (2 attempts) | |
| Core Keeper | 1 | 296s | |
| Project Zomboid | 1 | 372s | |
| Valheim | 7 | 197-579s | |
| Don't Starve Together | 1 | 701s (2 attempts) | needs a customer Klei token |
| ARK | 1 | 1269s | 22.9 GB SteamCMD download |
| Rust | 1 | 1475s (3 attempts) | |
| CS2 | 1 FAILED | 2062s | known-unsellable (66 GB install) |
| All `PROVISION` jobs | 51 DONE / 23 FAILED | p50 353s (DONE) | |

**35 of 35** "server ready" notifications in the 20 days before this fix read *"is up, with caveats …
guest agent has not answered yet"*.

### Bugs found and fixed (2026-10-01)

1. **The guest-agent wait could never succeed.** `waitForGuestAgent` polled `GET …/agent/ping`;
   Proxmox only defines `POST` for `ping` (`pvesh get …/agent/ping` → *No 'get' handler defined*).
   Every poll threw, so every provision waited the full 180s, returned `booted=false`, and told the
   customer "with caveats". The same function gates the password resync after `BACKUP_RESTORE` and
   `SNAPSHOT_ROLLBACK`, which therefore never ran. Now probes `GET …/agent/info` (a real guest-agent
   round trip) every 2s. **Expected effect: ~180s off every VPS provision, ~60-150s off every game
   provision, and honest "ready" notifications.**
2. **Minecraft heap = the whole VM.** The catalog's `-e MEMORY=2G` sets `-Xms`=`-Xmx`=2G; on the 2 GB
   plan the JVM cannot commit its heap without swap ("insufficient memory for the Java Runtime …
   failed to map 2147483648 bytes", crash loop, `NRestarts=78` in 10 min on a no-swap test VM); real
   orders survive only because of the swapfile. On the 8 GB plan the heap stayed 2G. Now
   `applyMinecraftHeap` sizes it to RAM minus max(768 MB, 25%) (2 GB → 1280M, 4 GB → 3072M, 8 GB →
   6144M) and clamps an explicit customer choice to that ceiling. *Not yet mirrored* in
   `worker/game-config.ts`'s post-provision MEMORY apply (R gamestate's area) — a customer who saves
   Settings can still re-apply an oversized value.
3. **Shared admin passwords.** Project Zomboid (`ADMIN_USERNAME=admin ADMIN_PASSWORD=changeme12`), ARK,
   ARK SA, Icarus, Soulmask, L4D2, TF2 shipped the same `changeme12` admin/RCON password on every
   server. Now: a blank customer value over a weak placeholder gets a per-server secret minted once in
   `provision()` and persisted into `Server.gameConfig` (visible in Settings, reused on retry and
   reinstall); admin/RCON env vars with no schema field are rotated per build. Join passwords are
   never touched. Platform RCON reads the password back out of the container env, so it keeps working.
4. **VMIDs were being recycled.** `/cluster/nextid` returns the lowest free id; node-5 destroyed 117 and
   142-145 overnight and handed 117/142/143 straight back out the same day. `allocateFreshVmid` now
   starts from `max(nextid, highest vmid ever on a Server row + 1, Setting vmid_high_water + 1)`,
   claimed atomically (one SQL upsert, safe under `WORKER_CONCURRENCY`), skipping 9000-9999, 200 and
   8000. The first allocation after deploy will be ~601 (current DB max is 600).
5. **Squad could never pass readiness**: `GAME_PORT.squad` was RCON 21114/tcp, which never opens without
   an RCON password. Now 7787/udp (with the in-guest bound-socket check). Found by the 2026-10-01 live
   all-families sweep.
6. **Silent heavy loads were declared stalled.** Squad/Stationeers had a flat disk and no log output
   for 3 minutes while loading. `waitOutGameInstall` now also counts the container cgroup's CPU time
   (≥15s CPU per 60s sample) as progress (`installProgressed`, `GAME_INSTALL_MIN_CPU_USEC`).
7. **Orders scheduled onto nodes without their template.** node-2/node-4 lack 9005-9009, node-5 lacks
   9001 and 9005-9009. `scheduleNode(…, { templateVmid })` now skips them (per-node template list,
   10-min cache, unknown = excluded, admin `logError` naming the nodes). Affected images: Debian 13 +
   Webmin/HestiaCP/CloudPanel (9001), Debian 12 (9005), Ubuntu 20.04 (9006), AlmaLinux 8 (9007),
   Rocky 8 (9008), Debian 11 (9009). **No game family is affected** (all clone 9000).
8. Smaller: game setup runs **before** the Claude CLI install (−10s); `get.docker.com` is skipped when
   Docker already exists (golden templates, `GAME_REINSTALL`); the primary's cloud-init snippets are
   written `0600` (they hold game secrets + the telemetry token; node-agent already did); the `set -x`
   setup log `/var/log/nxeon-setup.log` is pre-created `0600` (it echoes those secrets).

### Golden templates (opt-in, per family, per node)

A golden template = stock 9000 + `qemu-guest-agent`, `unzip`, `git`, `curl`, Docker CE and a few
pre-pulled images, with per-instance identity scrubbed (`cloud-init clean`, empty `/etc/machine-id`,
no SSH host keys, root password locked). A clone boots as a brand-new machine (verified: fresh
machine-id, fresh host keys, cloud-init sets the root password, `cloud-init status: done`).

**Measured, Minecraft 2 GB, node-2, same new snippet both times (from `qm start`):**

| | Stock 9000 | Golden 9101 |
|---|---|---|
| Guest agent | 117s | **15s** |
| SSH | 19.5s | 15.3s |
| Docker image ready | ~67s after setup start | **1.2s** |
| Game port open | 193s | **48s** |
| Clone (node-2) | 24.5s full | 67.7s full / **2.1s linked** |

End to end that is ≈ 220s → ≈ 50-60s with a linked golden clone (plus the 180s agent bug that both
columns no longer pay). Steam families gain proportionally less: their time is dominated by the
SteamCMD download inside the container, which a golden template cannot pre-seed without per-family
server files (see "Next steps").

**How provision() decides** (`chooseCloneSource`): `NXEON_GOLDEN_GAME_TEMPLATE` must map the order's
family to a vmid in 9100-9199 (`9101` = every game; `minecraft:9101,valheim:9101`; `*:9102` wildcard);
the order must be a game whose base is 9000; and the target node must have that vmid **as a template
tagged `nxeon-golden`** whose disk is not larger than the order's disk (Proxmox cannot shrink). Any
miss → stock 9000, logged per provision. Golden clones get a cloud-init snippet without the
`package_update`/`packages` block. `NXEON_GOLDEN_LINKED_CLONE=1` additionally makes golden clones linked
(`full: 0`) when the order's storage is the template's storage.

**Linked clones — the tradeoff.** ~2s instead of 25-70s and no extra space until the guest writes. But
Proxmox refuses to destroy a template that still has linked clones, so a rebuilt golden template always
gets a **new** vmid (9101 → 9102 …, as the never-reuse rule requires anyway), the env mapping is moved to
it, and the old one is destroyed only once `qm list`/`zfs list -t all` shows no clone depends on it.
Backups (`vzdump`) and restores produce independent full disks.

**Building one** (run ON the node, as root; never touches 9000/9001):

```
# 1. pick a vmid in 9100-9199 that has NEVER existed on ANY node (configs + /var/log/pve/tasks/index*)
# 2. pick a build IP 10.20.N.251-254 (outside the allocator pool) that does not answer ping
NXEON_FLEET_HOSTS="<the other 4 node IPs>" scripts/golden/build-golden-template.sh 9101 10.20.1.251 12G \
    itzg/minecraft-server:java21 itzg/minecraft-server:java25 lloesche/valheim-server
```

It clones 9000, boots it once with `scripts/golden/golden-build.yaml`, waits for the guest to power
itself off (25 min cap; on failure the VM is left for inspection), restores 9000's static vendor
`cicustom`, tags it `nxeon-golden`, converts it to a template and removes the build snippet. Disk: 12G
is needed for three images (Docker 29's containerd snapshotter stores compressed + extracted layers; a
6G attempt ran out of space). 12G excludes only plans smaller than that (Bedrock 5 GB, Necesse/CS 1.6
8 GB), which automatically fall back to stock.

**Distributing:** templates are per node. Either run the build script on each node (simplest — each
node gets an identical build), or `vzdump 9101` → copy → `qmrestore … <same vmid> --unique 0` +
`qm template`. Check the vmid fleet-wide first either way. Rebuild weekly (pre-pulled `:latest` images
and apt packages age; `docker create` uses the local image and does not re-pull) — build a new vmid,
move the env mapping, retire the old one when unreferenced.

**Current state (2026-10-01):** POC template **9101 exists on node-2 only** (`tpl-ubuntu-2404-game`,
12G, 4.24 GB used, MC java21+java25 + Valheim images). `NXEON_GOLDEN_GAME_TEMPLATE` is **unset in
prod**, so nothing uses it yet. Rollout = build on each node → set the env (start with
`minecraft:9101,valheim:9101`) → restart the worker → watch the `clone source` log line.

### Next steps (not built)

- **Per-family templates with pre-seeded server files** for the slow Steam families (Rust, ARK,
  Palworld, Valheim server files): a clone would only `steamcmd validate` a delta. Cost: the files live
  on every clone's disk and go stale with each game patch — needs a scheduled rebuild per family.
- **A local Docker registry mirror / Steam depot cache** per node (one pull per node instead of one per
  order). Lower risk than per-family templates; helps every family.
- **Pre-warmed spare VMs** (a booted golden clone per hot game per node, handed out on order): order to
  playable ≈ 10-20s, but each spare holds its RAM 24/7 (2 GB × 3 hot games × 4 nodes ≈ 24 GB of the
  fleet's ~280 GB), must be re-identified (hostname, password, keys, telemetry token) at hand-out, and
  is idle capacity that cannot be sold. Only worth it once golden + linked clones have shipped and the
  remaining ~50s is still the complaint.
- `qm resize` + config + start + NAT sync could overlap the clone wait on other nodes; small (<5s).

input.message:
## D2 provspeed: final report (stopped early because of the usage-window pause)

**Branch:** `feature/provision-speed-and-script-audit`. **Worktree:** `/opt/nxeon-wt-provspeed`. Everything is in one commit, `a0ac558f8b`. That commit is **not on GitHub yet**: no remote-tracking ref exists, so the post-commit push seems not to have run. I did not push by hand. Progress note: `/root/agent-notes/provspeed.md`.

### Timings (last 30 days of prod, run time not counting queue wait)
- **Plain Ubuntu VPS (n=13):** 193–264s. The Proxmox side (clone, config, start) takes about 16s of that.
- **Minecraft:** 199–262s. **Bedrock:** about 225s. **Valheim:** 197–579s.
- **Slower games:** Palworld 288/1177s, Project Zomboid 372s, ARK 1269s, Rust 1475s (3 attempts). CS2 failed.
- **Queue wait:** 0–40s, up to 137s before today's worker concurrency change.

**Biggest cause:** the worker waits for the VM's guest agent by calling an endpoint Proxmox doesn't have (`GET agent/ping`; ping is POST-only). Every provision therefore sat out the full 180s timeout. All 35 of 35 "server ready" notifications in the last 20 days said "with caveats". The same bug meant the password resync after a backup restore or snapshot rollback never ran.

Inside a stock VM, the first-boot apt update and package install alone take 72s.

### Proof-of-concept golden template
- **Built:** template 9101 on node-2: Ubuntu 24.04 with the guest agent, unzip, git, curl and Docker installed, plus the Minecraft (java21/java25) and Valheim images pre-pulled.
- **Measured (Minecraft, 2 GB, from VM start):**

| | Stock template | Golden template |
|---|---|---|
| Guest agent answers | 117s | 15s |
| Game port open | 193s | 48s |
| Clone on node-2 | 24.5s full | 67.7s full / 2.1s linked |

- **State:** it is opt-in and not switched on anywhere. Expected end to end is about 50–60s with linked clones, versus about 220s today.

### What changed
- **`lib/proxmox.ts`:** the agent check now uses `GET agent/info`, polling every 2s. New VM IDs now start above every ID ever handed out, so destroyed IDs are never recycled (node-5 was recycling 117/142/143 the same day).
- **`worker/index.ts` `provision()`:**
  - The game installs before the Claude CLI.
  - Golden clone source and linked clones, behind the env flags below.
  - New admin passwords are saved into the server's settings so the customer can see them.
  - Snippet files are now private (0600).
  - A retried provision no longer replaces the telemetry token of a VM that is already running.
  - The "still installing?" probe now also counts container CPU time.
- **`worker/game-variant.ts`:**
  - Minecraft heap is sized to the plan's RAM (2 GB plan gets 1280M).
  - The shared `changeme12` admin/RCON passwords (Zomboid, ARK, ARK SA, Icarus, Soulmask, L4D2, TF2) are replaced per server.
  - The Docker install is skipped when Docker is already there.
- **New files:**
  - `worker/cloud-init-parts.ts`: no package block on golden clones; setup log created private.
  - `lib/golden-template.ts`.
  - `lib/node-templates.ts`.
  - `scripts/golden/build-golden-template.sh` and `golden-build.yaml`.
- **Readiness check (`lib/games.ts`, `worker/provision-health.ts`):**
  - **Port fix:** Squad was checked on its RCON port (21114/tcp), which never opens; it now checks the game port, 7787/udp.
  - **No more false stalls:** container CPU time now counts as install progress, so slow, silent loads aren't judged stalled.
- **Docs and roadmap:** new docs section "Provisioning pipeline, timings and golden templates", a change-history entry, and ROADMAP updates.

### Files outside my area
- **Scheduler, at your request:** `lib/node-capacity.ts`, `lib/order.ts`, `lib/game-order.ts`.
- **Readiness check:** `lib/games.ts`, `worker/provision-health.ts`. Gamestate (R) has a branch titled "provision readiness", so expect merge conflicts there.
- **Tests:** `test/provision-health.test.ts`.

### Verification
- **Tests:** 107/107 passed. That run predates the last added test, the linked-clone one.
- **SQL:** the VM ID allocation query was checked on a throwaway DB, which has since been dropped.
- **Not verified:**
  - **Typecheck has not run.** The shared lock queue was about 25 deep and one attempt timed out. A second run is queued and writes to `scratchpad/tsc.log` and `test2.log`.
  - **No end-to-end provision through the real worker** with the new code, as you asked.
- **Cleanup:** all my benchmark VMs (77001–77006) are destroyed and their snippets removed.

### Your sweep questions
- **Missing templates:** debian-13 plus webmin/hestiacp/cloudpanel (9001) and the 9005–9009 images fail on the nodes that lack those templates. No game family is affected; all games clone 9000. The scheduler now skips nodes without the template.
- **Squad:** the port fix above is the fix.
- **Stationeers:** the image never binds a port (already documented); needs an owner decision.
- **Subdomain order failures** (enshrouded/gmod/tf2): the sweep harness isn't passing a subdomain. That's intended behaviour, not a bug.

### Needs the owner
1. Run the typecheck in the worktree and get the branch pushed.
2. Golden rollout:
   - Build the template on each node, after a fleet-wide VM ID check.
   - Set `NXEON_GOLDEN_GAME_TEMPLATE=minecraft:9101,valheim:9101`, optionally with `NXEON_GOLDEN_LINKED_CLONE=1`.
   - Restart the worker.
3. Gamestate (R) should apply the same heap clamp in `worker/game-config.ts`, or saving Settings can bring back an oversized heap.
4. Pin game images by digest: 44 of 49 game images run `:latest` or are untagged.
5. node-5's root disk is 96% full; it holds `/tank/backup` and is only 20G.
6. The auto-mode classifier blocked two read-only checks, which I did not pursue: a prod query of Minecraft heap settings vs plan RAM, and reading container-level ports on sweep VMs 142/143.

I've finished and sent the report. Two things aren't done: the typecheck never ran, and the work is committed (`a0ac558f8b`, branch `feature/provision-speed-and-script-audit`) but not on GitHub yet — the auto-push doesn't seem to have run.

**Main finding:** every provision waited a fixed 180 seconds for nothing. The worker checked the VM's guest agent with a request Proxmox doesn't support, so the check could never succeed. That is why a plain Ubuntu VPS took 193–264s when the Proxmox work is only about 16s. All 35 "server ready" notifications in the last 20 days said "with caveats". The same bug meant the password resync after a backup restore or snapshot rollback never ran. Fixed on the branch.

**Golden template test:** I built a test template (9101) on node-2 with the guest agent, Docker and the Minecraft/Valheim images already inside. On a 2 GB Minecraft server, timed from VM start:

| | Current template | Golden template |
|---|---|---|
| Guest agent answers | 117s | 15s |
| Game port open | 193s | 48s |
| Clone on node-2 | 24.5s | 67.7s full copy / 2.1s linked |

With linked clones a Minecraft order should take about 50–60s instead of about 220s. It is off everywhere until you set `NXEON_GOLDEN_GAME_TEMPLATE`.

**Other fixes on the branch:**
- **VM IDs:** IDs of destroyed servers were being handed straight back out (node-5 reused 117/142/143 the same day). New IDs now always go above every one ever used.
- **Minecraft memory:** the heap was a fixed 2G, so on the 2 GB plan Java claimed all the RAM and only ran by using swap. A test VM without swap crash-looped 78 times in 10 minutes, and 8 GB plans still only got 2G. The heap is now sized to the plan.
- **Shared admin passwords:** Project Zomboid, ARK, ARK SA, Icarus, Soulmask, L4D2 and TF2 all shipped the same `changeme12` admin/RCON password. Each server now gets its own, visible to the customer in Settings.
- **Squad:** the readiness check watched a port that never opens, so every Squad order failed. It now checks the real game port.
- **Slow game loads:** a slow, silent load (Squad, Stationeers) was judged "stalled". CPU use now counts as progress.
- **Scheduling:** orders are no longer placed on nodes missing their template. That affected Debian 13 plus Webmin/HestiaCP/CloudPanel, Debian 12, Ubuntu 20.04, AlmaLinux 8, Rocky 8 and Debian 11 on node-2, node-4 and node-5. No game family was affected.
- **Telemetry:** a retried provision permanently broke the server's telemetry; it now keeps the existing token.

**Testing:** 107 of 107 tests passed on a run before I added the last test. Nothing went through a real provision with the new code, because the coordinator was using node-5 for its own sweep. My test VMs are all destroyed.

**Needs you:**
- **Typecheck and push:** run `cd /opt/nxeon-wt-provspeed && npx tsc --noEmit -p .`, then get the branch pushed. The shared lock queue was about 25 deep and one attempt timed out.
- **Golden rollout:** build the template on each node (check the ID fleet-wide first), set `NXEON_GOLDEN_GAME_TEMPLATE=minecraft:9101,valheim:9101`, then restart the worker.
- **Saved Minecraft settings:** a customer saving Settings can still push an oversized heap. The fix belongs in `worker/game-config.ts`, which belongs to the gamestate agent. That agent's branch also touches the readiness check, so expect merge conflicts there.
- **Image versions:** 44 of 49 game images use `:latest` or no tag, so an upstream release can break new orders with no change on our side.
- **node-5 disk:** its root disk, which also holds `/tank/backup`, is 96% full.
- **Stationeers:** it never opens a port; that's a problem in its image and needs your decision.

The full write-up and the golden-template procedure are in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`, section "Provisioning pipeline, timings and golden templates". My progress note is `/root/agent-notes/provspeed.md`.
